text:
maya: Heads-up — ran into an odd edgecase in batch routing + telemetry. When we coalesce requests into 8k token batches the request-level scrubber sometimes sees concatenated context and misses PII split across boundary tokens. We end up with noisy sampled logs that still leak emails/names. anyone seen this?
sam: yep saw that in the canary last week. root cause: scrub runs before batching, so cross-request PII that spans boundary tokens survives.
jess: can we run the scrub after batching but before serialization to logs? that feels safer but perf cost might jump.
lee: post-batch scrub is safest for privacy but it complicates route-level sampling (we sample at request-level today). if we scrub after batch we lose mapping back to original request IDs for audit.
maya: exactly — audit/backfill needs linkability. we need to support both: strong redaction guarantees AND ability to reconstruct minimal audit trail when customers opt in.
product-ops: from UX: customers expect "inspect" toggles in console to let SREs view sampled payloads for debugging. how do we expose that without violating PII contracts?
jess: proposal: 1) canonical scrub pipeline run post-batch to guarantee no PII in general telemetry 2) optional per-request ephemeral tokens stored in a short-lived mapping (HMACed) that let authorized audit flows re-join requests to batches for a limited window 3) audit access gated via console RBAC and KMS unwrap.
sam: quick pseudocode to show idea:
```
# batch pipeline pseudocode
batches = batcher.collect(requests)
for b in batches:
  scrubbed = scrub(b)  # post-batch scrub removes cross-boundary PII
  log.emit(scrubbed)
  store_mapping_if_inspect_enabled(b.request_ids, hmac(scrubbed))
```
lee: storing mapping even HMACed might be unacceptable for some regs. need a consent flag per-customer and a per-route opt-in that defaults OFF. also TTL must be tiny (minutes).
product-ops: agree default OFF. we should show explicit warning in console when enabling inspect: "enabling inspect stores ephemeral mappings for X minutes and may include masked metadata".
qa-team: for tests we need fuzz cases where PII crosses tokens (emails split across wordpiece), multimodal inputs (image OCR text), and unicode normalization differences. can we add a unit test harness?
jess: yes — I'll add a test set: broken-email tokens, emoji in names, and multilingual names. we should also simulate high-throughput to measure latency diff post-scrub.
sam: perf numbers from quick bench: post-batch scrub + mapping ~ +7-12ms p95 on NVMe SSD-backed aggregator, but memory allocations for mapping add ~3% throughput cost.
maya: tradeoff seems acceptable if default OFF and only enabled for dedicated/debug routes. also need legal signoff on HMAC approach.
lee: ops asks: how do we integrate with current sampling? options: sample-before-batch (cheap, preserves request id), sample-after-batch (safer privacy), or hybrid where we sample both with different retention policies.
product-ops: hybrid sounds promising — sample-before for metrics only (no payload), sample-after for scrubbed payloads with tighter retention. console shows both lanes.
infra-bot: deploy: scrub-pipeline-v2 rolled to canary in us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T17:02Z :rocket:
maya: next steps: jess to prototype post-batch scrub + HMAC mapping, sam to add perf dashboard for canary, product-ops to draft console copy for inspect toggle, legal to review mapping plan.
product-ops: I'll queue a short modal copy and email CS template.
qa-team: I'll build fuzz harness and run against canary tomorrow.
lee: I'll put a hard TTL 5m default and add per-customer opt-out flag in routing policy.
maya: thanks all — let's sync in tomorrow's eng-platform standup. :thumbsup:
